prerequisites: ELEMENTS OF MECHANICS PROVIDED IN THE BASIC PHYSICS COURSE

learning_outcomes.text: The subject provides the basis for analyzing the dynamics of machines and mechanisms. Methodologies learned the student will be able to model the force fields acting on the system and understand the most suitable method for writing the equations of motion.

Knowledge and understanding of how to apply the methods learned the student will be able to choose which is the most suitable method, from a qualitative and quantitative point of view, to analyze the dynamical system behavior.
The student will be able to choose the parameters to be considered and which to neglect for an effective and efficient dynamic analysis of the system.
Knowing how to describe, in written form, clearly and concisely and exhibit orally with language properties the objectives, the procedure and the results of the processing carried out.
Being able to apply the knowledge acquired in contexts other than those presented during the course, and deepen the topics covered using materials other than those proposed.

syllabus_topics: WRITING OF THE EQUATION OF THE MOTION OF A POINT MASS, SUBJECTED TO AN ELASTIC AND GRAVITATIONAL FIELD, EXPRESSED IN A NON-INERTIAL REFERENCE SYSTEM.
WRITING OF THE MOTION EQUATION OF A RIGID BODY, SUBJECTED TO THE ACTION OF ELASTIC FIELDS, GRAVITATIONAL FIELDS, AND EXTERNAL FORCES, EXPRESSED IN A NON-INERTIAL REFERENCE SYSTEM.
ROTORS WITH GYROSCOPIC STRUCTURE. EULER EQUATION MODIFIED. EXERCISES.
DYNAMIC EFFECTS DUE TO GYROSCOPIC INERTIA TORQUES ON A WIND TURBINE WITH TWO BLADES.
SIMPLE PENDULUM. EQUATION OF MOTION USING LAGRANGE AND CARDINAL EQUATIONS; EQUILIBRIUM POSITIONS; LINEARIZATION AROUND THE EQUILIBRIUM POSITION; STABILITY.
MASS-SPRING MODEL. EQUATIONS OF MOTION; SOLUTION WITH HARMONIC FORCING. INFLUENCE OF INITIAL CONDITIONS ON SYSTEM RESPONSE.
MASS-SPRING SYSTEM RESPONSE TO ANY FORCER.
EQUIVALENCE BETWEEN SECOND-ORDER DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS AND FIRST-ORDER SYSTEMS. EXERCISES ON CONSERVATIVE SYSTEMS TO A DEGREE OF FREEDOM, FREE AND FORCED.
GEOMETRIC REPRESENTATION OF THE REPOSITORY OF A MASS-SPRING-DAMPING SYSTEM IN THE PHASE PLANE. FIRE POINTS, KNOT, CENTER, AND SADDLE.
RESPONSE OF AN OSCILLATOR TO ONE DEGREE OF FREEDOM.
CONSERVATIVE VIBRATING SYSTEMS WITH TWO DEGREES OF FREEDOM.
FREE RESPONSE OF A SYSTEM IN THE PRESENCE OF A VISCOELASTIC FIELD: COMPARISON BETWEEN THE MAXWELL AND KELVIN MODEL.
DYNAMIC ANALYSIS OF THE SUSPENDED MASS WITH SPRINGS HOWEVER ARRANGED.
FORCED FREE VIBRATIONS OF A BEAM.
CYLINDRICAL BEARING: SHORT AND LONG MODEL.
MECHANICAL CLUTCH COUPLINGS. CONE CLUTCH CLUTCHES.
YIELD OF MACHINES IN SERIES AND PARALLEL. DEGREE OF IRREGULARITY DURING THE PERIOD.
BODY ON A HORIZONTAL AND INCLINED PLANE. LOCKING DEVICE. TAPE BRAKE.
MOTORCYCLE OF AN UPHILL VEHICLE. BALL-BALL ROLLING; BALL-PLATE.
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written and an oral test. The examination commission determines the final grade based on the preparation demonstrated in both tests. Honours are awarded to candidates who show excellent preparation on all course topics.
